translations.literal: The Geographical Records of the Han shu took over Qin’s thirty-six commanderies and several hundred counties and towns; later they were gradually subdivided until, by the time of Emperor Ping, there were 103 commanderies and kingdoms and 1,587 counties, towns, roads, and marquisates in all.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu’s Geographical Records in the Han shu began from the thirty-six Qin commanderies and ended at Ping’s tally of 103 commanderies and kingdoms and 1,587 county-level units.

sentences.zh: 世祖中兴，惟官多役烦，乃命并合，省郡、国十，县、邑、道、侯国四百余所。

translations.literal: When Emperor Guangwu restored the dynasty, offices were many and corvée burdens heavy, so he ordered mergers and abolitions, cutting ten commanderies and kingdoms and more than four hundred counties, towns, roads, and marquisates.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu’s reunification forced wholesale consolidation: ten commanderies and kingdoms and over four hundred lower seats vanished from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 至明帝置郡一，章帝置郡、国二，和帝置三，安帝又命属国别领比郡者六，又所省县，渐复分置。

translations.literal: By Emperor Ming one commandery was added; by Emperor Zhang two commanderies or kingdoms; by Emperor He three more; Emperor An again ordered six dependent states to rank alongside commanderies, and counties that had been abolished were gradually split out again.
translations.idiomatic: Later emperors partly reversed the cuts: Ming added one seat, Zhang two, He three, and An raised six dependent states to parity with commanderies while old counties crept back onto the map.

sentences.zh: 至于孝顺，凡郡、国百五，县、邑、道、侯国千一百八十，民户九百六十九万八千六百三十，口四千九百一十五万二百二十。

translations.literal: By the Shun and Emperor Huan reigns there were 105 commanderies and kingdoms, 1,180 counties, towns, roads, and marquisates, 9,698,630 registered households, and 49,150,220 persons.
translations.idiomatic: By Shun and Huan the empire again held 105 commanderies and kingdoms, 1,180 county-level units, and census figures just under 9.7 million households and 49.15 million people.

sentences.zh: 赞曰：众安后载，政洽区分；

translations.literal: The encomium says: The people were at peace in later reigns, and government harmonized as the map was carved into commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: The stanza opens by praising the post-restoration order: settled subjects and a bureaucracy that could actually mark off each jurisdiction.

translations.literal: Marquises were abolished and prefects arrayed in their stead, so the people had no hereditary local lord.
translations.idiomatic: The old Warring States pattern of a fixed prince gave way to rotating Han magistrates.

translations.literal: Designations shifted from age to age, and partitions of fiefs bred endless quarrels.
translations.idiomatic: Each generation renamed and re-cut territories until the genealogy of seats read like a lawsuit.

translations.literal: We set down in outline what was cut or added, for the most part corroborating earlier accounts.
translations.idiomatic: The compiler’s apology: a lean gazetteer, but one that usually checks out against the older histories.
